x: Gibberellin causes bolting by driving rapid internode elongation in rosette plants just before flowering. Auxin acts mainly in tropisms and apical dominance, cytokinin in cell division, and ABA inhibits growth.
t: Link bolting and dwarf-to-tall growth with gibberellin.
s: Which plant hormone causes bolting, the sudden elongation of the stem in rosette plants such as cabbage?

x: ABA stands for abscisic acid, the plant stress hormone that closes stomata and keeps buds and seeds dormant.
t: Recall the expansion of ABA.

x: ABA is the stress hormone: it builds up in drought and closes stomata to save water. Auxin, gibberellin and cytokinin promote growth.
t: Discriminate growth promoters from the growth inhibitor.

x: Option C is incorrect: ABA inhibits growth and promotes dormancy. Auxin, gibberellin and cytokinin all promote growth.
t: Discriminate growth promoters from the growth inhibitor.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: tropisms come from auxin moving to one side of a shoot; rooting is a separate effect.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a parallel effect.

x: Both are true and R explains A: gibberellin triggers enzymes that start germination, which is how it breaks seed dormancy.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: ABA closes stomata, cutting water loss through transpiration.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: cytokinin regulates growth by promoting cell division and keeps leaves green longer by delaying senescence.
t: Recall the functions of cytokinin.

x: Statement A is true: auxin promotes rooting, as in rooting powders. Statement B is false because germination effects belong to gibberellin.
t: Discriminate auxin effects from gibberellin effects.

x: Auxin causes apical dominance, gibberellin stem elongation, cytokinin delays senescence and ABA closes stomata, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.

x: Auxin promotes rooting, gibberellin breaks dormancy, cytokinin drives cell division and ABA gives drought tolerance, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.

x: Auxin drives tropisms, gibberellin causes bolting, cytokinin promotes cell division in tissue culture and ABA acts as an antitranspirant, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
 a. Auxin
 b. Gibberellin
 c. Cytokinin
 d. ABA

List-II
 i. Antitranspirant
 ii. Bolting in rosette plants
 iii. Promotes cell division in tissue culture
 iv. Tropic growth responses

x: I, II and III are correct: auxin promotes growth, apical dominance and rooting. IV is false because delaying senescence is cytokinin's job.
t: Discriminate auxin from cytokinin.
s:
Consider the following statements about auxin:
I. It promotes growth.
II. It is associated with apical dominance.
III. It influences rooting.
IV. It delays senescence.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: I, II and III are correct: gibberellin elongates cells and stems and aids germination. IV is false because closing stomata is ABA's job.
t: Discriminate gibberellin from ABA.
s:
Consider the following statements about gibberellin:
I. It is associated with cell elongation.
II. It promotes stem elongation.
III. It has seed germination-related effects.
IV. It causes temporary closure of stomata.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Three belong to ABA: drought tolerance, stomatal closure and growth inhibition. Delaying senescence is cytokinin.
t: Recall the functions of ABA.

x: All four are correct: auxin drives tropisms, gibberellin breaks dormancy, cytokinin drives cell division and ABA is an antitranspirant.
t: Recall the function of each plant hormone.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Auxin is associated with tropic growth responses.
II. Gibberellin can help overcome dormancy.
III. Cytokinin promotes cell proliferation.
IV. ABA acts as an antitranspirant.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Ethylene (C₂H₄) is the only gaseous plant hormone, which is why one ripe fruit can ripen others nearby.
t: Recall ethylene as a gas.

x: Ethylene triggers the respiratory climacteric, the burst of respiration during the ripening of fruits such as banana and mango.
t: Recall the functions of ethylene.

x: Option C is incorrect: ethylene (as ethephon) stimulates latex flow in rubber trees. It promotes leaf and flower fall and senescence.
t: Recall the commercial uses of ethylene.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: fixing CO₂ into sugars is where the energy ends up; the conversion itself happens when chlorophyll captures light.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a related step.

x: I and II are correct: photosynthesis occurs in green parts, in chloroplasts. III is false because the stroma hosts the dark reaction; the light reaction is in the thylakoids.
t: Discriminate thylakoid (light) from stroma (dark) reactions.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Photosynthesis occurs in the green parts of a plant.
II. The chloroplast is the organelle associated with photosynthesis.
III. The stroma is the site of the light reaction.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: I and II are correct: oxygen is a by-product, and CO₂ is fixed into organic compounds. III is false because of "only"; glucose is stored as starch or sucrose.
t: Check each statement for the word "only".
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Oxygen is a by-product of photosynthesis.
II. Carbon dioxide is converted into organic compounds.
III. Glucose is stored only as sucrose.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: At plant level photosynthesis is in green parts, the main organ is the leaf, the tissue is mesophyll and the organelle is the chloroplast, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the levels of photosynthesis.

x: The light reaction runs on thylakoid membranes and the Calvin cycle in the stroma, both inside the chloroplast, the organelle of photosynthesis. The mitochondrion is the site of aerobic respiration. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Place light and dark reactions inside the chloroplast, and respiration in the mitochondrion.
s:
Match the cell location in List-I with the process or role in List-II.

List-I
 a. Thylakoid membrane
 b. Stroma
 c. Chloroplast
 d. Mitochondrion

List-II
 i. Organelle of photosynthesis
 ii. Dark reaction/Calvin cycle
 iii. Light reaction
 iv. Site of aerobic respiration

x: Chlorophyll is the main pigment, it absorbs light, mainly red and blue, and reflects green, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall why leaves look green.

x: All four are ethylene effects: it ripens fruit, forms root hairs, inhibits stem and root elongation and stimulates latex flow in rubber.
t: Recall the functions of ethylene.
s:
How many of the following are functions or effects of ethylene?
1. Fruit ripening
2. Root hair formation
3. Inhibition of stem and root elongation
4. Latex flow in rubber

x: All four are correct: glucose is the main product, stored as starch or sucrose, oxygen is a by-product and light becomes chemical energy.
t: Recall the products of photosynthesis.

x: Red light is the most effective for photosynthesis, absorbed strongly by chlorophyll. Green is mostly reflected.
t: Recall the action spectrum of photosynthesis.

x: Chlorophyll is located in the chloroplasts, in their thylakoid membranes. Mitochondria carry out respiration.
t: Recall where chlorophyll is located.

x: Chlorophyll is green because it absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
t: Recall the colour of chlorophyll.

x: Chlorophyll has magnesium at its centre, haemoglobin iron and vitamin B₁₂ cobalt, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Recall the central metal of each molecule.

x: Both are true and R explains A: chlorophyll captures light energy, so photosynthesis cannot happen without it.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The Krebs cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix, glycolysis splits glucose into two pyruvate, yeast fermentation yields ethanol and CO₂, and the electron transport chain sits on the inner mitochondrial membrane, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall where each stage of respiration happens and what it produces.
s:
Match the respiration process in List-I with its site or feature in List-II.

List-I
(a) Krebs cycle
(b) Glycolysis
(c) Alcoholic fermentation by yeast
(d) Electron transport chain

List-II
(i) Produces ethanol and carbon dioxide
(ii) Inner mitochondrial membrane
(iii) Mitochondrial matrix
(iv) Splits glucose into two pyruvate molecules

Codes:

x: I and II are correct: stomata are in the leaf epidermis, each a pore with guard cells. III is false because mitochondria are organelles, not where stomata are.
t: Recall the location of stomata.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Stomata are located in the leaf epidermis.
II. A stoma has a pore and guard cells.
III. Stomata are located primarily in mitochondria.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All four are stomatal functions: gas exchange, letting in CO₂, letting out O₂ and transpiration.
t: Recall the functions of stomata.

x: Both are true and R explains A: when guard cells swell with water the pore opens, and when they go limp it closes.
t: Check whether R is the mechanism of A.

x: I, II and III are correct: stomata carry out transpiration, potassium ions drive guard-cell swelling, and ABA closes stomata in drought. IV is false because stomata have guard cells.
t: Recall the mechanism of stomatal opening.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Stomata are involved in transpiration.
II. Potassium is important in stomatal opening and closing.
III. ABA promotes stomatal closure under water stress.
IV. Stomata consist only of a pore and have no guard cells.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Mg is the symbol for magnesium, the central atom of chlorophyll. Fe is iron, Co cobalt and Cl chlorine.
t: Recall element symbols.

x: Option C is incorrect: most transpiration happens through stomata in leaves; roots absorb water. Transpiration is loss of water vapour.
t: Recall the route of transpiration.

x: Both are true and R explains A: water evaporating from leaves pulls water up the xylem, which is the transpiration pull.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Transpiration cools leaves as water evaporates and takes heat with it, preventing overheating.
t: Recall the functions of transpiration.

x: Transpiration drives upward water transport and carries minerals from root to shoot. It does not form stomata or move minerals downward.
t: Recall the functions of transpiration.

x: Both are true and R explains A: ABA closes stomata, which cuts water loss.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Xerophytes such as cacti have thick cuticles, sunken stomata and reduced leaves, all of which reduce transpiration in dry places.
t: Recall the adaptations of xerophytes.

x: I and II are correct: nitrogen drives growth and is part of proteins, chlorophyll and nucleic acids. III is false because nitrogen is a macronutrient.
t: Discriminate macronutrients from micronutrients.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Nitrogen is associated with plant growth and development.
II. Nitrogen is associated with proteins, chlorophyll and nucleic acids.
III. Nitrogen is a micronutrient.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Phosphorus is part of ATP and nucleic acids and promotes root development. The "only" options are too narrow.
t: Recall the role of phosphorus.

x: Both are true: potassium regulates stomatal opening, and calcium builds cell walls and activates enzymes.
t: Recall the role of K and Ca.

x: Sulphur is part of amino acids such as cysteine and methionine and is needed for chloroplasts and nitrogen fixation.
t: Recall the role of sulphur.

x: Iron is needed for chlorophyll synthesis and electron transport, and boron for meristem growth and nodule formation, giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Recall the role of each micronutrient.

x: Zinc is needed to make tryptophan, from which auxin is formed, and copper is part of plastocyanin in photosynthetic electron transport, giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Link zinc with auxin synthesis and copper with plastocyanin.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Zn
(b) Cu

List-II
(i) Part of plastocyanin in photosynthetic electron transport
(ii) Needed to make tryptophan, the precursor of auxin

Codes:

x: Manganese supports photosynthesis and enzymes, and molybdenum supports nitrogen metabolism (nitrogenase), giving a-ii, b-i.
t: Recall the role of each micronutrient.

x: Both are true: chlorine and nickel are both micronutrients, needed only in tiny amounts.
t: Recall the micronutrients.

x: Three are macronutrients: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Iron is a micronutrient.
t: Discriminate macronutrients from micronutrients.

x: Three are micronutrients: iron, boron and zinc. Magnesium is a macronutrient.
t: Discriminate macronutrients from micronutrients.

x: Excessive transpiration causes water loss and can lead to wilting. Nodules, roots and nitrogen metabolism are unrelated.
t: Recall the effect of excessive transpiration.
